about: The only quotes a theme page may show, each read against its source before it was added. Fields and checks: src/lib/themeQuotes.ts. A page draws its block from the entries that list it, in the order they stand here.

quotes.text: Let it make no difference to thee whether thou art cold or warm, if thou art doing thy duty; and whether thou art drowsy or satisfied with sleep; and whether ill-spoken of or praised; and whether dying or doing something else.
quotes.rights: Public domain. George Long's translation was first published in 1862.

quotes.text: Since it is possible that thou mayest depart from life this very moment, regulate every act and thought accordingly.
quotes.rights: Public domain. George Long's translation was first published in 1862.
quotes.checked: Project Gutenberg ebook 15877, footnote marks left out

quotes.text: They thought I was a Surrealist, but I wasn't. I never painted dreams. I painted my own reality.
quotes.rights: Kahlo died in 1954. The English wording is the magazine's, one remark quoted with its source.

quotes.text: All deities reside in the human breast.

source.author: William Blake
source.work: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
source.line: _The Marriage of Heaven and Hell_ (1790 to 1793), plate 11

quotes.rights: Public domain.
quotes.checked: Project Gutenberg ebook 45315. The quote opens in mid-sentence, the capital is ours.

quotes.text: Everything harmonizes with me, which is harmonious to thee, O Universe. Nothing for me is too early nor too late, which is in due time for thee.
quotes.rights: Public domain. George Long's translation was first published in 1862.

quotes.text: Unless there is death, there cannot be birth.

source.author: Joseph Campbell
source.line: _The Power of Myth_, episode 4, “Sacrifice and Bliss” (PBS, 1988)

quotes.rights: Campbell died in 1987, so the series is in copyright. One short sentence, quoted with its source.

quotes.text: Till this moment, I never knew myself.
quotes.speaker: Elizabeth Bennet
quotes.rights: Public domain.

quotes.text: To deny people their human rights is to challenge their very humanity.

source.author: Nelson Mandela
source.work: address to the Joint Session of the United States Congress
source.line: address to the Joint Session of the United States Congress, 26 June 1990

quotes.rights: Mandela died in 2013, so his speeches are in copyright. One sentence from a public address to a parliament, quoted with its source.

quotes.text: I had reasoned this out in my mind; there was one of two things I had a right to, liberty, or death; if I could not have one, I would have the other.

source.author: Harriet Tubman
source.work: Harriet, the Moses of Her People
source.line: as told to Sarah H. Bradford, _Harriet, the Moses of Her People_ (1886), spelling standardised, sentence shortened

quotes.rights: Public domain. Bradford's book was published in 1886.
quotes.checked: Project Gutenberg ebook 9999, which prints her speech in dialect spelling

quotes.text:
In every cry of every man,
In every infant's cry of fear,
In every voice, in every ban,
The mind-forged manacles I hear:
quotes.rights: Public domain.
quotes.checked: Project Gutenberg ebook 574, the text of the poem page on this site

quotes.text: The most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious. It is the source of all true art and science.
quotes.rights: Einstein died in 1955. Out of copyright in Germany since 2026, and this 1930 printing in the United States since 2026.
quotes.checked: archive.org, scan of the Forum and Century printing (item what-i-believe-albert-einstein-1930)

quotes.text: I am a feather on the breath of God.

source.author: Hildegard of Bingen
source.line: from a letter to Odo of Paris, about 1148, shortened

quotes.rights: Hildegard died in 1179. The line is the short form in which modern English renders a longer passage of the letter.

quotes.text:
The Imagination is not a State: it is the Human Existence itself.
Affection or Love becomes a State when divided from Imagination.
quotes.rights: Public domain.
quotes.checked: Wikisource, page scan of The Prophetic Books of William Blake: Milton (1907), page 51

quotes.text: The person, be it gentleman or lady, who has not pleasure in a good novel, must be intolerably stupid.
quotes.speaker: Henry Tilney
quotes.rights: Public domain.

quotes.text:
Love is the astrolabe of God's mysteries.
A lover may hanker after this love or that love,
But at the last he is drawn to the KING of Love.

quotes.text: There is nothing either good or bad but thinking makes it so.
quotes.speaker: Hamlet
quotes.rights: Public domain.
quotes.checked: Project Gutenberg ebook 100, the text of the quotes page on this site. The quote opens in mid-sentence, the capital is ours.

quotes.text: All dein Tun und Denken sei so beschaffen, als solltest du möglicherweise im Augenblick aus diesem Leben scheiden.

quotes.text: Ich habe meinen Zug nie entgleisen lassen und niemals einen Passagier verloren.
quotes.rights: Public domain. Tubman died in 1913. The German is our own translation of a remark she made in 1896.

quotes.text: Es gibt eine Hartnäckigkeit in mir, die es nie ertragen kann, durch den Willen anderer eingeschüchtert zu werden. Mein Mut wächst stets mit jedem Versuch, mich einzuschüchtern.
quotes.speaker: Elizabeth Bennet
quotes.rights: Public domain. The German is our own translation.

quotes.text: Wenn es keinen Tod gibt, kann es keine Geburt geben.

source.author: Joseph Campbell
source.line: _The Power of Myth_, Folge 4 (PBS, 1988), eigene Übersetzung

quotes.rights: Campbell died in 1987, so the series is in copyright. One short sentence in our own translation, quoted with its source.

quotes.text: Die Imagination ist kein Zustand: Sie ist die menschliche Existenz selbst. Zuneigung oder Liebe wird zu einem Zustand, wenn sie von der Imagination getrennt ist.
quotes.rights: Public domain. The German is our own translation.

quotes.text:
Höchste Güte ist wie das Wasser.
Des Wassers Güte ist es,
allen Wesen zu nützen ohne Streit.
Es weilt an Orten, die alle Menschen verachten.
Drum steht es nahe dem Sinn.

quotes.text: Ich bin eine Feder im Atem Gottes.
